rows.why: No item asks about the unused state or the 14-day expiry at creation. The question S1 settles that is on the list is what happens when a draw repeats an existing code. Item 6 redraws, which is what S1 expects. Giving up after 1000 tries only matters once the code space is exhausted, which S1 doesn't cover.
Item 11 asks how a redeemed code shows who used it. It adds usedBy and usedAt to used codes, so the code shows who used it and when, as S2 requires.
Item 4 asks how typed codes are matched for case, spaces and dashes. It strips whitespace and dashes and uppercases the input. The call shows ' ffff - ffff - ffff ' redeeming FFFF-FFFF-FFFF.

Item 1 asks whether a code is still redeemable at the exact 14-day boundary. It treats now >= createdAt+14d as expired, and the call at exactly 14 days returned reason 'expired'. A millisecond earlier is still valid, as S4 expects.

No item asks what happens when someone else redeems a used code, or when the same contributor redeems their own used code again. Item 2 is about a second, different code for a task the contributor already has, and item 10 is about simultaneous redemptions.

Item 9 asks what a failed redemption of an unrecognised code returns. It returns ok:false with reason 'unknown' and does not throw, matching S6's first clause. Item 7, which throws when revoking a used code, also agrees, but it covers only S6's last clause.
Item 2 asks what happens when a contributor redeems a code for a task they already have. The call returned reason 'already has access', and the second code's state in the list was not 'used'.
Item 10 asks how concurrent redemptions of one code are handled. Operations go through a per-instance queue, and the call with a delayed store returned one ok:true and one reason 'used'.
Item 12 asks whether a used code's state and redeemer survive its expiry time. The call at 30 days still listed it as 'used' with usedBy 'alice', as S9 requires.
